messages:
ravi (Eng): Heads up team: I'll be splitting weeks between Philly and NYC for a client pilot starting 2025-03-03. It's not a permanent move, more like 3 days in Philly / 2 days in NYC each week. Do I need to declare? :thinking:
maya (People Ops): Thanks for flagging. Split-week patterns can create dual-state payroll exposure. Please fill the temporary homebase form so payroll/tax vendor can evaluate nexus. Link: https://hr.redwood.example/homebase-declare
ravi (Eng): Filing now. Quick Q: is the WFH stipend prorated for split-weeks or stay with home state?
ellen (Finance): Stipend is prorated by days worked in each state. For recurring split-week patterns we look at the typical calendar over the payroll period. We'll calculate exactly after we see your calendar pattern for the pay month.
ravi (Eng): Calendar will show recurring Mon-Wed Philly, Thu-Fri NYC.
maya (People Ops): Important: For multi-state work every week, payroll often flags nonresident withholding in both states. For PA/NY that could mean registering for withholding in PA. Payroll will advise.
sam (Manager): Sam here I reviewed the pilot and approve. Ravi, make sure client-side docs allow you to work from both locations. No objections from me.
ravi (Eng): Thanks Sam. Also planning to pick up office laptop from NYC office and leave it in Philly for the week. Is that allowed?
logistics-bot: Short-term equipment relocation domestic: covered up to $60/month for temporary storage/shipping. Please open equipment ticket and tag it "split-week storage". Attach manager acknowledgement.
ravi (Eng): Created EQ-9911 and attached Sam's message.
logistics-bot: EQ-9911 received. Please include secure storage address and expected pickup/return cadence.
maya (People Ops): Also note worker comp usually remains tied to your permanent homebase. But if you spend significant time in another state we may need to evaluate. For split-week, we will flag to Legal if >30% of your working time moves to a secondary state.
ellen (Finance): We'll run a 3-month projection based on your declared schedule. If PA withholding is required we'll notify you and HR will coordinate any registrations. Expect payroll review within 4 business days after form submission.
ravi (Eng): Form submitted. hr-bot: "homebase-declare" form submitted by ravi at 2869998888. Next: People Ops review -> Payroll/TAX review -> Equip ticket EQ-9911 processing.
maya (People Ops): Thanks Ravi. Please keep calendar invites transparent so payroll can verify actual days if needed. We'll post an update here once payroll completes review.
ellen (Finance): Follow-up: based on initial review, PA nonresident withholding may be required; we'll post exact percentages and take-home impact by 2869998925.
ravi (Eng): Appreciated. One last thing  will this affect my state benefits or retirement contributions?
maya (People Ops): No change to benefits enrollment or 401k location for a split-week pilot. Those remain tied to your permanent homebase. If anything changes long-term we'll re-evaluate.
hr-bot: Payroll review opened (PR-20256). Estimated update by 2869998925.
